title: Gingerbread Icebox Cake
changes_from_base: Gingersnaps layered in a loaf tin with a treacle and spice whipped cream, frozen and coated in crushed gingersnaps, instead of sponge and ice cream.
summary: Spiced whipped cream is layered with crunchy gingersnaps and frozen into a loaf, then coated all over with crushed gingersnap crumbs for a warming, spiced dessert.
equipment: stand mixer or hand mixer with whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip the 680 g double cream on medium until it reaches the thickness of yoghurt, 2-3 min, then add the 140 g black treacle, 1 tbsp ground ginger, 2 tsp ground cinnamon, ½ tsp fine salt, 1 tsp vanilla paste, ½ tsp nutmeg and ½ tsp black pepper and whip to thick, medium peaks, 1-2 min.

steps.title: Line
steps.text: Brush the loaf tin with water and line with cling film, leaving an 8 cm overhang.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Spread 240 ml of the spiced cream up the sides of the tin and 180 ml over the base.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Add a layer of the 450 g gingersnaps broken to fit, then 180 ml more cream, and repeat the layers up to the rim, finishing with a little extra cream on top.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Fold the film over the top and freeze for at least 2 h, keeping back any leftover cream and biscuits.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Invert the cake onto a plate and peel off the film.

steps.title: Decorate
steps.text: Pipe the reserved cream into any cracks and smooth, then crush the remaining gingersnaps and press them over the cake to coat, brushing the plate clean.

tips: Whip the cream to thick, medium peaks so it holds the biscuit layers together once frozen.
Keep back some cream and biscuits to patch and coat the cake once it is turned out.
Add white chocolate chips as an optional decoration if you like a little extra sweetness.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 1 month.
